title: Phosphate–vitamin D coupling does not improve temporal prediction of parathyroid hormone beyond flexible standard measures
abstract: A literature-led serum phosphate-by-log25OH-vitaminD interaction was evaluated in 4162 NHANES2003–2004 adults and 4087 separately sampled2005–2006 adults. Weighted ridge models included flexible standard mineral, renal and demographic measures. Target weighted log-PTH RMSE was 0.379518 without and 0.379534 with the interaction; baseline-minus-augmented gain -0.00001624 (joint PSU bootstrap95% interval -0.00036219 to 0.00011220). Source PSU-held-out cross-validation likewise did not favor the interaction. This is a negative predictive result for one prespecified feature, not evidence against mineral endocrine feedback or proof of equivalence. Validation is temporal within NHANES, not across unrelated study programs; these cycles were previously used for other questions.
